title: Cascade failover flipbook
body:
Purpose: quick, messy chronicle of the cascade failover playtests I ran on 2026-01-28 -> 2026-03-09. Not formal runbook; notes to self and scribbles for Priya/Jorge.

Summary of problem observed:
- Intermittent 503 spikes for region eu-west-1 clients between 02:10-02:40 UTC on 2026-02-26.
- Traffic should have hit fallback regional pool (eu-west-2) but instead some requests were routed to the global low-priority pool and hit cold-starts (strong CPU thrash + high tail latency).
- Symptoms: latency > 2s for streaming start, token latencies high, and increased KV-cache misses.

Quick timeline (local repro attempts):
- 2026-02-27 09:12 local fliptest: started synthetic load against route policy A (policy-A: prefer-local -> cross-region fallback -> global-burst).
- 2026-02-27 09:17 observed policy controller report: region health degraded eu-west-1 -> flagged as \"degraded\" but not \"unavailable\". Router still sent 60% of traffic to eu-west-1 for ~3 minutes.
- 2026-02-27 09:21 manual promote: forced eu-west-2 primary via route-probe override; tail latency dropped after ~18s.

Commands I ran (warts included):
- Route probe check:
  curl -s -X GET \"https://route-controller.internal/api/v1/policies/policy-A/status\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN\" | jq .
  -> status.showing: {\"eu-west-1\": \"degraded\", \"eu-west-2\": \"healthy\"}  (note: controller packaged output is messy)

- Grepped logs for 503 signature:
  kubectl -n route-ctrl logs -l app=router --since=1h | rg \"503.*fallback.*kv-miss\" -n || true
  sample: 2026-02-26T02:15:04Z router-7f6f 503 route=policy-A src=euw1-conn1 fallback=global-burst kv_cache=miss token_ms=322

- Verified KV cache stats on edge hosts (redis proxy):
  telnet redis-proxy-euw1 6379
  > INFO keyspace
  # hits: 122  misses: 98
  -> Miss rate ~44% under load; this seems too high compared to normal ~8-12%

Reproduction notes (what I did to force the cascade):
- Step 1: Artificially delayed kube-probe responses for a small subset of backend pods (sleep 6 instead of 1s) using a temporary debug sidecar.
- Step 2: Simulated transient packet loss on the eu-west-1 egress path (tc qdisc netem loss 5%).
- Step 3: Started a blended client profile (50% short-chatter, 50% long-stream) at 200 rps from eu-west-1 available load generator.
- Observed: policy-A marked partial degradation; router attempted local retries (3x) then applied fallback. But fallback selection favored global-burst pool rather than pinned eu-west-2 because global-burst had stale score and an aggressive score-decay window (configured to 10m).

Error snippets (copied raw):
- router: \"WARN route-decider: fallbackPick failed heuristic=stale-score fallback=global-burst because score.timestamp older-than window=600s\"
- controller: \"ERROR policy-sync: inconsistent-region-list for policy-A: eu-west-2 not present in local cache\"
- worker: \"KVCacheMiss: key=prefix:conv:abc123 hit=false backend=redis-proxy-euw1\"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Score decay configuration too conservative. When eu-west-2 recently accepted burst traffic, its score didn't refresh quickly enough and global-burst (older score but higher ephemeral score) got chosen.
2) Partial controller cache inconsistency between route-controller replicas. A leader briefly had eu-west-2 and others didn't, leading to split-brain decisions during the 3-minute window.
3) High KV cache miss rate on eu-west-1 made local attempts very expensive (extra backend calls) so router fallback heuristic penalized local options.
4) Retry policy ordering currently does retries -> fallback; maybe we need to try fallback earlier for streaming requests to avoid rehydration cost.

Experiments I ran to test hypotheses and quick results:
- Rapid score-refresh: lowered score-decay window from 600s -> 30s in a test cluster (policy-A-test). Result: immediate shift to eu-west-2 when flagged; tail latency reduced, but we saw some oscillation (flip-flop) at high rps. Suggests fast refresh helps but requires stability guards.
- Controller cache reconciliation: forced full-sync every 15s on a replica; result: replicas aligned and split-brain window disappeared in test. CPU overhead marginal.
- Early-fallback path: modified local router to allow 1 early fallback for streaming-start-only (no additional retries). This improved cold-start token latency by ~25% in the controlled test.

Open questions / next steps (for sprint ticket):
- Is it safe to reduce score-decay across all policies? Need rate-limit to avoid oscillation. Consider hysteresis: require new-score > old-score + delta to override.
- Investigate root cause of KV cache miss spike on eu-west-1 (was it a memory pressure event? eviction? network partition?). Check host-level dmesg and oom logs.
- Add a short-term controller health broadcast (small gossip heartbeat) so replicas can converge faster than full-sync windows.
- Consider changing fallback ordering logic to be latency-aware for streaming-start vs token continue. Separate heuristics for short vs long lived requests.

Notes to Priya / Jorge:
- Priya: saw you added a canary for early-fallback in your branch; let's pair on adding hysteresis logic so it doesn't oscillate.
- Jorge: can you take a quick look at redis-proxy metrics around 2026-02-26 02:00-03:00 UTC? Link I used in tests: http://grafana.internal/d/redis/redis-proxy?from=1677408000000&to=1677411600000

Random debugging crumbs (for myself):
- When I saw \"fallback=global-burst kv_cache=miss\" repeated, check router backoff timers in /var/log/router/backoff.log — found one entry where backoff timer was stuck at 120s after an earlier misinterpreted 502.
- Useful quick command to simulate streaming start without full client:
  python -c \"import requests; r=requests.post(\'https://api-staging.internal/v1/stream?route=policy-A\', headers={\'Authorization\':\'Bearer stub\'}, json={\'prompt\':\'short\' }, stream=True); print(r.status_code)\"

Appendix: configuration snippets I toggled (for reference)
- policy-A score-decay: 600s -> temporary test 30s
- route-decider params: retries=3 -> temp=1 for streaming-start early-fallback test

Closing note: this flipbook is intentionally messy. The big thread is: stale routing scores + controller cache windows + local KV miss penalty combined to produce an unexpected cascade to global pool. Fix plan: short-term early-fallback for streaming-start (with hysteresis), medium-term reduce score-decay + stability guard, long-term stronger controller convergence + better KV cache visibility.

-- DS
